review_cost.rationale: I'd approve after one round of small, well-scoped changes: abortSignal, the dead dependency, the load-state boundary, and the fragment edge. Nothing requires rearchitecting.

findings.issue: PokeApi.get ignores the resource loader's abortSignal; resource() cancels loads via AbortSignal on param change/destroy, but the underlying fetches keep running.
findings.suggestion: Accept an AbortSignal in get() and pass it to fetch; thread resource loaders' abortSignal through loadPokemonView/loadMoveTables/loadHomeData.

findings.issue: Moves tables fan out one request per learned move (100+ for popular Pokémon) with no cancellation when the user switches game, only the 5-minute cache as protection.
findings.suggestion: Plumb abortSignal through, and consider batching/deduplicating at the API layer or loading move details lazily per visible table.

findings.issue: A shared component imports pages/not-found, inverting the shared→pages boundary and creating a cycle risk.
findings.suggestion: Move NotFound into shared/ (it is a presentational placeholder, not a routed page body).

findings.issue: The #fragment scroll effect runs once per component instance: reading ActivatedRoute.snapshot.fragment at construction and a 'jumped' flag mean later same-route navigations with a fragment never scroll, and a moves error skips the jump entirely.
findings.suggestion: Track the current fragment reactively (e.g. via router events or a query param input) and re-arm the jump per navigation, or enable withInMemoryScrolling({anchorScrolling: 'enabled'}) and handle the late-render case on top of it.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is declared but never imported; the app uses native form elements.
The promise cache checks TTL on read but never evicts expired entries, so a long session grows the Map toward one entry per API resource.
findings.suggestion: Delete expired entries on read (cheap since the Map is scanned anyway) or cap its size.

findings.issue: fs.createReadStream(file).pipe(res) has no 'error' handler; a file disappearing between stat and read becomes an unhandled stream error that can crash the server.
findings.suggestion: Attach stream.on('error', ...) that destroys the response, or read the file with fsp.readFile.

findings.issue: All styling is global, with selectors like '.site-main > :not(router-outlet)' and '.site-main app-not-found' coupling global CSS to specific routed components — renaming a component selector silently breaks layout.
findings.suggestion: Move per-component rules into the components' own scoped styles (styles/styleUrl), keeping only base/layout in the global sheet.

findings.issue: The missing-sprite fallback mutates the DOM directly in the event handler (style.visibility), a small home-grown workaround.
findings.suggestion: Track failed ids in a component Set and hide via a template binding/class so the change detection round-trip stays declarative.

summary: A current-idiom Angular 22 app: resource()-based loading, @Service(), signal inputs and native control flow, with clean core/pages/shared layering and unusually good error handling (typed 404s, per-request fallbacks, real HTTP 404s from the custom server). The issues I'd flag are all small: no abortSignal plumbing despite documented guidance, a shared→pages import inversion, a one-shot fragment-scroll effect, an unused dependency, and global CSS that reaches into routed components. I'd merge after one round of nits.
